name: Pose-free and Feed-forward Training

# Pose-free and Feed-forward Training

Also called: Feed-forward 3DGS, Generalizable Gaussian Splatting

## Overview
This family reconstructs 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) scenes from uncalibrated or sparse image collections without relying on external [Structure-from-Motion](#16341-structure-from-motion-sfm.md) pipelines [G]. It sets itself apart from traditional 3DGS by eliminating iterative pose estimation, and from feed-forward alternatives by either initializing Gaussians via foundation model priors [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md) or jointly optimizing poses as learnable parameters [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md). Builds on [Learning and Training Methods](9068-learning-and-training-methods.md).

## Shared principles
All methods in this family rely on [differentiable rendering](#16276-differentiable-rendering.md) to compute gradients from the rendered image to the Gaussian parameters (position, covariance, opacity, [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md)) and/or network weights [G]. The rendering process remains differentiable with respect to the scene representation [G]. Loss functions typically combine photometric reconstruction error, such as $\mathcal{L}_{L1}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{MSE}$, with perceptual or structural metrics like $\mathcal{L}_{MS-SSIM}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{LPIPS}$ [G].

## Subtopics

### [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md)
[InstantSplat](#6136-instantsplat.md) is a pose-free, sparse-view [3D Gaussian Splatting method](#4010-gaussian-kernel-volumetric-primitive.md) that eliminates the need for Structure-from-Motion pipelines by leveraging geometry priors from foundation models like MASt3R or VGGT [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md). It enables training in seconds by directly initializing Gaussians from these priors, distinguishing itself from feed-forward methods which regress primitives directly from images, and from traditional 3DGS which requires dense pose estimation [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md). Choose this method when rapid reconstruction from very sparse views (3–10 images) is required without iterative optimization [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md).

> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```python
def instant_splat(input_images, intrinsics):
    depth_maps, relative_poses = extract_priors(input_images)
    point_cloud = back_project_depth(depth_maps, intrinsics, relative_poses)
    gaussians = initialize_gaussians(point_cloud)
    for step in range(num_steps):
        rendered_images = render(gaussians, relative_poses)
        loss = compute_loss(rendered_images, input_images)
        gaussians = optimize(gaussians, loss)
    return gaussians

def back_project_depth(depth_maps, intrinsics, relative_poses):
    points = []
    for depth, pose in zip(depth_maps, relative_poses):
        for v in range(depth.shape[0]):
            for u in range(depth.shape[1]):
                z = depth[v, u]
                x = (u - intrinsics.cx) * z / intrinsics.fx
                y = (v - intrinsics.cy) * z / intrinsics.fy
                points.append(pose @ np.array([x, y, z, 1]))
    return np.array(points)
```

### [AnySplat](6137-anysplat.md)
[AnySplat](#6137-anysplat.md) is a pose-free feed-forward network that reconstructs 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from uncalibrated image collections without requiring camera pose annotations [AnySplat](6137-anysplat.md). It predicts 3D Gaussian primitives and per-image intrinsics and extrinsics in a single forward pass [AnySplat](6137-anysplat.md). Unlike sibling methods, it scales to casual dense or sparse multi-view captures, matches pose-aware baselines, and surpasses prior pose-free methods in zero-shot evaluations at real-time rendering latency [AnySplat](6137-anysplat.md). Choose this method when handling arbitrary multi-view captures where pose data is unavailable and real-time inference is needed [AnySplat](6137-anysplat.md).

### [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md)
pixelSplat is a feed-forward model that reconstructs a 3D radiance field parameterized by 3D Gaussian primitives from a pair of input images, enabling real-time and [memory-efficient rendering](#1547-batched-ray-rendering.md) [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md). It solves the problem of local minima inherent to sparse, locally supported representations in generalizable novel view synthesis, where non-differentiable pruning or splitting cannot be applied because gradients must back-propagate through the representation [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md). Unlike light-field transformers which produce black-box ray colors, pixelSplat generates an explicit, editable 3D representation [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md). Choose this method when working with stereo pairs and requiring an explicit, editable 3D representation with real-time rendering [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md).

> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```python
def pixelsplat_forward(image_pair, camera_params):
    features_resnet = [resnet50_dino(img) for img in image_pair]
    features_vit = [vit_b8_dino(img) for img in image_pair]
    features_sum = [f_res + f_vit for f_res, f_vit in zip(features_resnet, features_vit)]
    epipolar_features = epipolar_cross_attention(features_sum[0], features_sum[1], camera_params[0], camera_params[1])
    prob_dist = predict_probability_distribution(epipolar_features)
    sampled_depths = sample_from_distribution(prob_dist)
    ray_origin, ray_direction = camera_params[0].origin, camera_params[0].direction
    sampled_means = ray_origin + sampled_depths * ray_direction
    gaussian_params = []
    for u in pixels:
        F_u = get_pixel_feature(epipolar_features, u)
        phi, delta, Sigma, S = neural_network_f(F_u)
        gaussian = Gaussian(mean=sampled_means[u], covariance=Sigma, opacity=phi, scale=S)
        gaussian_params.append(gaussian)
    rendered_image = gaussian_splatting_rasterize(gaussian_params, camera_params[0])
    return rendered_image, gaussian_params
```

### [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md)
[Joint Pose Optimization](#6888-joint-pose-optimization.md) refers to methods that simultaneously optimize camera poses and the scene representation to eliminate the dependency on pre-computed Structure-from-Motion pipelines [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md). This approach relaxes the strict requirement for known camera parameters, allowing novel-view synthesis from unposed images using only photometric loss [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md). It distinguishes itself from pose-free feed-forward methods by iteratively refining poses during training rather than predicting them in a single forward pass, though it typically requires rough initialization and is limited to small motions [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md). Choose this method when iterative refinement is acceptable and camera motions are relatively small, avoiding the need for a trained feed-forward network [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md).

### [Loss Scheduling for Candidate Head](13095-loss-scheduling-for-candidate-head.md)
Loss scheduling for the candidate head is a training strategy that gradually reduces the influence of an image-dependent 'candidate head' ($\hat{C}_i$) during optimization, transitioning to a shared representation ($\hat{C}$) to stabilize pose estimation for hard-pose images [Loss Scheduling for Candidate Head](13095-loss-scheduling-for-candidate-head.md). It prevents the shared representation from being distracted by wrong supervision introduced by hard-pose images in the early stages, allowing the model to assimilate these images into the shared representation once the shared model is accurate enough [Loss Scheduling for Candidate Head](13095-loss-scheduling-for-candidate-head.md). This method is distinct from sibling methods by explicitly decoupling the training influence of per-image heads via a cosine schedule rather than relying solely on joint pose optimization or fixed head structures [Loss Scheduling for Candidate Head](13095-loss-scheduling-for-candidate-head.md). Choose this method when training models with per-image candidate heads to stabilize pose estimation for challenging or hard-pose images [Loss Scheduling for Candidate Head](13095-loss-scheduling-for-candidate-head.md).

> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```python
def compute_loss_schedule(l, u, v, loss_shared, loss_candidate):
    if l < u:
        w = 0.0
    elif l < v:
        w = 1.0 - (math.cos(math.pi * (l - u) / (v - u)) / 2.0)
    else:
        w = 1.0
    scheduled_loss = w * loss_shared + (1.0 - w) * loss_candidate
    return scheduled_loss
```

### VS-Splat Extension for Noisy Camera Poses
An extension to handle noisy camera poses, following the SHARE implementation with a modified input module [S1, unofficial]. It uses three 1×1 2D convolutional layers to reduce the channel dimension of feature maps from 768 to 128, matching the SHARE input dimension, with each convolutional layer preceded by a normalization layer and a Swish activation [S1, unofficial]. Due to GPU memory constraints, the number of fine-grained primitives per voxel $M$ is set to 8 [S1, unofficial]. On the CO3D dataset, this extension yields a PSNR of 21.62, SSIM of 0.864, and LPIPS of 0.211 [S1, unofficial]. Choose this variant when the input camera poses are noisy and require robust feature alignment similar to SHARE [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The family originates from the need to generalize 3D Gaussian Splatting beyond single-scene optimization, which is computationally expensive and requires accurate initial poses [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md). Early work like [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md) introduced feed-forward architectures to predict Gaussian primitives directly from image pairs, addressing the local minima issues of traditional [splatting](#23-splatting.md) [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md). Subsequent developments like [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md) and [AnySplat](6137-anysplat.md) incorporated foundation model priors to enable pose-free reconstruction from sparse or uncalibrated views, significantly reducing training time to seconds [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md), [AnySplat](6137-anysplat.md). [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md) provides an alternative by treating poses as learnable parameters rather than predicting them via a network [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md). These methods are used in generalizable novel view synthesis, 3D object reconstruction from sparse views, and applications requiring real-time rendering from casual captures [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md), [S1, unofficial].
